overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on the three complaint allegations (notice specificity, undisclosed documents, inaudible breakouts, no YouTube broadcast), but flagged its own concern about post-it note exchanges as possible serial deliberation and issued only a reminder.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the March 21, 2023 joint meeting notice was insufficiently specific because it did not disclose scenario planning led by a facilitator.
allegations.key_passage: We are satisfied that the topic as listed on the notice here was sufficient to reasonably advise the public of the issues to be discussed at the meeting, that is, ways to control the beach erosion along Sconset Bluff

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the joint meeting failed to post documents corresponding to the noticed topic (the three erosion control scenarios).
allegations.key_passage: In addition, the Board and Commission were not required to post attachments pertaining to the topic listed on the notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that the Board and Commission breakout group discussions on the three scenarios were not audible to attendees, making portions of the meeting inaccessible.
allegations.key_passage: However, we do not find a violation of the Open Meeting Law here because none of the three groups contained a quorum of Board or Commission members.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the joint meeting was not broadcast via YouTube; the meeting was open in person and streamed on Zoom.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board and Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law where it provided both in-person access and access through the web-based Zoom platform, without also providing access via YouTube.

allegations.summary: Not raised by the complaint; the AG flagged concern that post-it note opinions on the scenarios may have reached a quorum serially outside a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Although each of the three breakout groups contained less than a quorum of Board or Commission members, the opinions shared via the post-it notes likely reached a quorum of Board or Commission members in a serial manner as the groups rotated between the three scenarios.
